svg.title: openstack-multitenant-reference: architecture
svg.desc: Source of architecture-topology.png, shown in docs/concepts/architecture.md. After editing this file, render the PNG at twice the size with a headless Chrome or Chromium, from this directory: chromium --headless --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --window-size=1720,1540 --screenshot=architecture-topology.png architecture-topology.svg Keep --window-size equal to the width and height of the svg element.
svg.text: One project per role; each joins the networks it uses through its own router; every target admits only declared sources
public addresses of the entry point, egress of the shared services
egress, and public addresses of tenants exposed directly · input egress_network
may be the same external network as below
may be the same external network as above
bastions, Kubernetes API and bootstrap · input admin_network
may be the network of the internal services plane
The entry point opens to the tenants’ service addresses
Consumers open to the providers of internal services
Every project pushes metrics, logs and audit events
load balancer · one public IP, many domains
SNI reverse proxy × 2 · no TLS key
e.g. network services: resolvers, time, mirrors, egress proxy
proxy: through the internal services plane
Who admits what: the isolation matrix (docs/reference/isolation-matrix.md).
Only declared sources and ports are admitted; a route alone opens nothing.
bastion: simplified; it has its own network, a router to the administration network and a port on the project’s network
a project’s router on a network, named after it; below: its role on a plane, or its use of an external network
shared = offers a service on the plane · tenant = uses it · a router exists only if the project uses that network
dashed router or arrow: optional, or the alternative path (direct exposure) · dashed project: optional, or an alternative
no route between two tenants; a tenant offering a service to others takes the role shared on a plane
